name: Philippe de Champaigne

summary.text: Philippe de Champaigne was a Brabant-born French Baroque era painter, a major exponent of French Baroque painting. He was a founding member of the Académie royale de peinture et de sculpture in Paris, the premier art institution in the Kingdom of France during the Ancien Régime.

3226347: The Feast in the House of Simon the Pharisee is a c.1656 oil on canvas painting by Philippe de Champaigne, now in the Fine Arts Museum of Nantes. It was commissioned around 1656 by Queen Anne of Austria, wife of Louis XIII.
The Feast in the House of Simon the Pharisee (Champaigne)
3873328: Vanitas, also known as Allegory of Human Life or Still Life with a Skull, is an oil on panel painting attributed to Philippe de Champaigne, from 1667. It is held in the musée de Tessé, in Le Mans, which bought it at a public auction in 1884.
5419125: Ex-Voto de 1662 is a painting by the French artist Philippe de Champaigne now in the Louvre in Paris.
15707397: Portrait of Cardinal Richelieu is an oil on canvas painting by Philippe de Champaigne, from c. 1635-1640. It is one of the 21 portraits he produced of cardinal de Richelieu.
15707415: Louis XIII Crowned by Victory is a 1635 oil on canvas painting by Philippe de Champaigne. Probably commissioned by Cardinal Richelieu, it shows Louis XIII, King of France, crowned by a personification of Victory to mark his forces' victory in the Siege of La Rochelle.
20054113: The Triple Portrait of Cardinal de Richelieu is an oil-on-canvas painting by French artist Philippe de Champaigne, completed c. 1642. The portrait shows Cardinal Richelieu from three angles: right profile, face on, and left profile.
Triple Portrait of Cardinal de Richelieu
23005278: The Tribute Money is an oil on canvas painting by the Flemish-French painter Philippe de Champaigne, created c. 1663–1665. It is held at the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts.
26492852: Portrait of Cardinal Richelieu is one of 21 surviving oil on canvas portraits of Cardinal Richelieu by the French painter Philippe de Champaigne. Produced in 1633–1640, it is now in the National Gallery, in London, to which it was presented by Charles Butler in 1895.
26713584: The Dream of Saint Joseph is an oil painting on canvas by Philippe de Champaigne, now in the National Gallery, London, which bought it in 1958. It measures 209.5 × 155.8 cm, and probably dates to 1642–1643.
38520998: Portrait of Cardinal Richelieu is a portrait painting of Cardinal Richelieu by the Flemish-born French painter Philippe de Champaigne, Richelieu's favourite portraitist. It was painted a few months before the cardinal's death, in 1642, and is now in the Musée des Beaux-Arts of Strasbourg, France.
56305179: Elijah's Dream is an oil on canvas painting by Philippe de Champaigne, from c. 1650-1655. It is held in the musée de Tessé in Le Mans A similar earlier work by the artist is his 1642 The Dream of Saint Joseph for the Chapelle des Minimes de la place Royale.
72296975: The Nativity is an oil on canvas painting by Flemish-French Philippe de Champaigne, created c. 1643. It has been in the Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille since 1804.
83742678: Christ Healing the Blind is an oil on canvas painting by Philippe de Champaigne, painted from c. 1655 to 1660. It is held at the Timken Museum of Art, in San Diego.
112056949: Moses and the Tablets of the Law is a 1663 oil on canvas painting by Philippe de Champaigne, now in the Musée de Picardie in Amiens, to which it was given in 1922 by Alexis Marie François de Boutray.
Moses and the Tablets of the Law
115675911: Assumption of the Virgin is an oil on canvas painting by Philippe de Champaigne, from 1638. It depicts the assumption of Mary, now in the Museum of Grenoble.
115676120: The Raising of Lazarus is a 1633 oil painting on canvas by the French painter Philippe de Champaigne, on long-term loan from the Louvre to the Museum of Grenoble, which also holds that artist's The Assumption, to which it was a pendant.
121071421: Madonna and Child or Madonna with the Sleeping Christ Child is a c.1654-1655 oil on canvas work by Philippe de Champaigne, now in the Musée des Beaux-Arts d'Agen in Agen.
